shortDescription: Shares of Signet Jewelers NYSE:SIG jumped about 12% in premarket trading on Wednesday after the jewelry retailer reported second-quarter adjusted earnings well above expectations and raised its full-year profit outlook.Adjusted earnings were $2.19 per share, above the $1.73 Bloomberg consensus esti…

children: jumped about 12% in premarket trading on Wednesday after the jewelry retailer reported second-quarter adjusted earnings well above expectations and raised its full-year profit outlook.

Adjusted earnings were $2.19 per share, above the $1.73 Bloomberg consensus estimate. Sales of $1.53 billion were broadly in line with the $1.53 billion estimate, while same-store sales rose 2.2%, ahead of the 1.7% consensus, helped by growth across its fine jewelry brands.
North America comparable sales rose 1.9%, slightly above the 1.8% estimate, while international comparable sales increased 6.0%, topping the 2.84% estimate.
The stronger profit reflected several factors. Average unit retail prices increased about 6%, while gross margin expanded 80 basis points to 39.4% of sales. Signet

also received about $15 million in tariff refunds, $13 million more than it had expected, while lower inventory and distribution costs also supported margins. Higher gold costs partly offset those benefits.

SG&A fell to 32.3% of sales from 32.9% a year earlier, with the company citing operating-model changes and sales growth for the leverage. Adjusted operating income rose to $107.2 million from $85.4 million as gross margin expanded and selling, general, and administrative expenses declined as a percentage of sales.
raised its fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS forecast to the midpoint of $11.30, which is about 4.5% above the $10.81 Bloomberg consensus.

The company kept its full-year sales outlook at $6.8 billion at the midpoint, broadly in line with the $6.83 billion consensus, while raising its adjusted operating income guidance to $570 million at the midpoint, from $520 million previously.
expects sales of $1.39 billion at the midpoint, in line with the $1.39 billion Bloomberg estimate.
also authorized a $125 million accelerated share repurchase and increased its remaining buyback authorization to about $700 million.
Shares are down 0.25% YTD, significantly underperforming the broader index, which has gained about 12% during the same period. Short interest on SIG stands at 13.02% of the total float.

title: Signet Jewelers jumps as profit beats estimates, full-year outlook raised
